venue: Proceedings of the IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR)

A shared schedule observed in a particular retained run is a configuration/result, not the whole algorithm's definition. Proxy rescaling is not a claim that cached residual outputs are necessarily rescaled.

title: Validity of the Single Processor Approach to Achieving Large Scale Computing Capabilities
venue: Proceedings of the April 18–20, 1967, Spring Joint Computer Conference
verified_claim: The part of a workload that is not accelerated limits overall speedup; the report applies this established principle to measured denoising time and the remaining generation cost.
verification_notes: Verified author, title, conference, year, pages and DOI against the indexed ACM DOI landing page; a direct reopen returned HTTP 403.
Read the original paper scan at https://www.cs.cmu.edu/~18742/papers/Amdahl1967.pdf. Its discussion of unavoidable sequential/housekeeping work supports the limiting-speedup principle.

The displayed S(r) equation and the numerical 2.75 limit are this project's elementary specialization to its measured timing boundary, not numerical results reported by Amdahl and not a novel cost law.
